proposal.title: 100-Coin daily commitment prototype
principles: Reserve new expedition direct Coins, full pouch value and maximum possible positive cosmetic salvage before launch. Establish any reduced direct amount before the child commits; never trim a claim.

Reserve a random activity pouch's full face value before granting it. Only candidates whose full value fits the remaining allocation are eligible before the draw; never grant a partial pouch or reroll saved loot.
Each child's new commitments reset daily without banking unused allowance. Redemptions may exceed 100 Coins on a later day because previously established rewards are paid in full.
Preserve owned pouches, frozen expedition loot and authored challenge promises. Fixed authored rewards stay outside this proposed random-grant allocation and must be reported separately.
Track reserved, paid and outstanding Coin values separately, along with empty item slots, zero-Coin expeditions and permanently unavailable content.

blockers.title: Evaluate the prototype against explicit targets
blockers.detail: The Lab now separately models the 75/25 allocation, fixed expedition rewards and full-value pouch reservations. The income-envelope candidate remains a separate policy that omits payout excess.
blockers.next_action: Save paired 90-day and 365-day comparisons with income, purchasing and content-access targets; record the design decision and affected acquisition paths before implementing live rules.

blockers.title: Preserve every established reward
blockers.detail: The in-memory model pays established rewards fully. Production has no corresponding reservation protocol; existing pouch stacks read shared item definitions rather than a per-unit face-value snapshot.
blockers.next_action: Specify versioned reward definitions and reservation records; test full redemption, late claims, retries, concurrent launches and the accounting of outstanding promises.

blockers.title: Specify Lucky Coin timing
blockers.detail: Live Lucky Coin can double direct expedition Coins at claim. Consumable effects are excluded from both Lab policies, so neither candidate proves a live maximum payout.
blockers.next_action: Decide when boosted value is established and reserved, then simulate and test activation, expiry and delayed claims without changing prior promises.

blockers.title: Check pouch and collection access
blockers.detail: The prototype reports filtered grants and unavailable finite targets because full-value reservations change acquisition paths. Missing paths are not additional playable runway, and source-level availability does not guarantee timely completion.
blockers.next_action: Audit every affected acquisition path, first-reward pacing, empty returns and collection milestones; use the content workbench for new reward versions and a reviewed code change for expedition policy.

inputs.name: 100-Coin starting experiment
inputs.hypothesis: Test income and first-reward pacing before changing live grants.

modeled: New child with zero XP, Coins and owned companions/inventory
Reading, approved synthetic chores, positive synthetic habits, project time, journal, creations and movement
Supported drops use current rarity tier budgets, authored within-tier weights and unowned cosmetic priority
Parallel automatic catalog challenges, guaranteed companion trails and eligible badge criteria
Hatching, rarity/authored food growth, evolution and bounded mount expeditions with same-trip cosmetic duplicate avoidance
Opt-in anonymous real-world reward and print purchases, calendar cost/resource budgets, assumed wages and parent-approved money-to-Coins top-ups
Hypothetical shared per-child daily Coin income envelopes for expeditions, expedition salvage and opened Coin pouches
Opt-in fixed 100-Coin new commitment experiment: 75 expedition and 25 random activity-pouch Coins, preserving full established rewards
Shared optional per-child expedition launch and whole-item promise quotas, independent of the Coin policy
excluded: Homework, completed projects/milestones, savings, actual cash payments/bonuses, birthdays and grade progression
Private family chores, habits, reward offers/budgets and redemptions; digital shop fulfillment, parent goals and co-op/legacy quests
Consumable use and XP/Coin/drop/growth boosts; consumable drops remain held inventory
Perfect Day, manual grants, time-of-day and approval-delay effects
Unmodeled badge criteria and cosmetic equipping; cosmetic-only starter cover gift
Production deployment/asset delivery verification and player retention/engagement predictions
assumptions: Day 1 starts an abstract week; visits occur on the first N days of each seven-day block
All configured chores are approved that visit; each habit is a distinct positive habit with one tap/day
Source skills are fixed synthetic tags, reported in activity_skills; absent/locked skills earn no XP
Care hatches any compatible new pair, opens Coin pouches and feeds all available food to the oldest unevolved pet
Expeditions launch at the end of a visit and are claimed on the next active visit after return
New source events advance every matching challenge; challenge duration is a deadline, not a minimum wait
Percentile days are calendar days conditional on completion; unreached trials remain in completion_rate
Finite content counts modeled badges, one-off challenges, obtainable cosmetic identities and companion stages only; it is not total app runway
Remaining finite targets means uncompleted, including missed one-off deadlines; expired unfinished challenges are reported separately and are not future playable content

summary.percentile_basis: Calendar days among trials completing within the horizon; completion_rate includes every trial

audit.message: This forecasts the stated activity/care policy, not full app exhaustion or measured retention.
No private reward offers are read. Coins accumulate; shop affordability and economic balance require a separate spending assumption.
There is no assumed starter pet or guaranteed egg/potion. First hatch depends on the loaded eligible sources and random draws.
First companion is reached in 33% of these trials within the horizon. Inspect ingredient supply and care policy.
First grown companion is reached in 33% of these trials within the horizon. Inspect ingredient supply and care policy.
6 finite targets belong to this modeled source subset. Unmodeled badges and activities are not treated as consumed.

assumptions: This is a hypothetical reduction in new-child Coin income, not a live reward rule. Each trial is an alternative history of one child.

One shared envelope covers direct expedition Coins, expedition cosmetic salvage and all opened Coin pouches, regardless of pouch origin. Other Coin sources, XP and item rolls retain their installed rules.
The envelope resets each simulation calendar day. Unused allowance is not banked; inactive days do not increase the next visit's budget. Null means uncapped and zero omits all included Coins.

Included awards use first-arrival order: expedition claims precede activity and end-of-visit pouch opening. All mounts share the same child's allowance; earlier rewards can leave no allowance for later pouches.

Excess included Coins are omitted, never deferred or owed. Synthetic pouches are still consumed and expedition items retained. This must not be applied retroactively to owned pouches or already committed live expedition loot.
Raw Coins are the included awards encountered within each policy's simulated journey, not a paired uncapped counterfactual. Coin-related progression changes can alter later eligibility and rewards.
Summary and source percentiles are calculated independently across alternative trials; use means or individual trial values to reconcile source totals.
This anonymous experiment changes only new synthetic expedition launches and item promises. No live expedition, reward rule or inventory is changed.
One child's mounts share the daily launch and item allocations. Null means unlimited, zero prevents the selected new commitments, and unused capacity never banks across calendar days.

Requested trips are the configured count at each active visit. Eligible trips are the smaller of that request and currently available mounts. Prevented trips are eligible trips withheld by the launch quota; unavailable mounts are reported separately.

Nominal item slots are counted only for launched trips. Before drawing loot, the remaining item quota bounds whole slots; each successfully selected item consumes one unit, including pouches and cosmetics later salvaged. Empty eligible pools do not consume item capacity.

Slots requested equal slots promised plus nominal slots withheld by the quota plus permitted slots left unfilled by the eligible pool or Coin commitment policy. Withheld nominal slots are not a counterfactual count of items that would have dropped.

Item-only quotas still allow later Coin-only trips. The Coin commitment policy may also promise zero direct Coins; zero-item, zero-Coin and fully empty trips remain visible rather than being silently skipped.

A saturated day exactly uses an allocation on a relevant eligible opportunity; a limited day actually withholds a trip or nominal slot. Zero allocations do not count idle or no-mount days as saturated. Each day counts at most once per measure.

Frozen loot claims retain their complete item and Coin promises. Claimed and pending items count promised units, including later salvage, not retained inventory. Grandfathered units lack a new-budget reservation marker and are reported separately.
For new-budget promises, slots promised equal claimed items minus grandfathered claimed items plus pending items minus grandfathered pending items. Claims do not consume a later day's allocation.

The unlimited finite denominator removes both expedition quotas while retaining the same Coin policy and routine. Unavailable targets are excluded acquisition paths, not extra playable runway; this loss cannot be added to the separate Coin-policy comparator.

Authored challenge items, activity drops, boosts and future launch/claim concurrency are outside these expedition slot quotas. This is a design comparison, not a live reservation protocol or retention prediction.
